story: At 3:17 on this humid, hazy Sunday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at the Rec Center telling Donna he'll give her twenty minutes of his time and asking her to go easy on his knees. Donna, eager for company, is looking around for someone to talk to while she waits for him. Back at his porch, Hal sits content in his chair with his notebook closed, keeping his word to stay off it until Monday and looking forward to Rosa's table tonight. Rosa, also content, is in her kitchen packing up dinner leftovers and tidying up.
events: Donna waited: looking around for someone to talk to
Hal waited: Resting in the porch chair with the notebook closed, keeping my word until Monday and looking forward to Rosa's table tonight.
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Pack up dinner leftovers and tidy the kitchen

gary.thought_process: Donna just walked in and we came here so she could coach me on pickleball. I've already looked over the ladder board while waiting, and I haven't actually said anything to her yet this tick. She dragged me out here out of kindness, and honestly it feels good to have someone care. The cart can wait; the lights get shown off once Architectural Review signs off. Best move is to greet her, take her up on the lesson, and get on the court.

parameters.content: Well, you made it, Donna. Alright, I'm all yours for twenty minutes. Just go easy on my knees and don't tell Hal how bad I am.

donna.thought_process: Gary and I both made it to the rec center, and the courts are wide open on a Sunday afternoon. I invited him out here to get him hitting, and I shouldn't keep chatting when there's a ladder to climb. Court reservations max out at 2 hours under L-05, so I'll keep it short and sweet: get him on court one, show him a dink, and start building this partnership.

parameters.content: looking around for someone to talk to

donna.engine_note: tried to speak to None, who isn't here

hal.thought_process: It's a hazy Sunday afternoon and nobody is within sight. I gave my word to keep the notebook closed until Monday, and I've been sitting on this porch for hours doing just that. The binoculars and notebook can stay where they are. Rosa's dinner is tonight, and I'd rather arrive in a good mood than with a list of grievances. No reason to go stirring things up. I'll rest in the chair and let the day run out.

parameters.content: Resting in the porch chair with the notebook closed, keeping my word until Monday and looking forward to Rosa's table tonight.

rosa.thought_process: I've written the coffee-with-Hal note into my shift schedule over and over in recent ticks. Tick 408 even spelled out 'Coffee with Hal, Tuesday 9 AM' in pen, and the reflection says it finally feels real. The dinner went well and everyone's here in spirit. Nobody is nearby, it's a hazy Sunday afternoon, and there's nothing left to re-ink. Rather than keep looping on the schedule, I should do something different and useful. I'll go to the kitchen and start on leftovers and get the house back in order, which also gives me a quiet hour to feel good about having finally built a table full of neighbors.

parameters.content: Pack up dinner leftovers and tidy the kitchen

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
